name: pspy - Unprivileged Linux Process Monitoring
description: pspy monitors Linux processes in real-time without root. Uses inotify on /proc to detect new processes, including cron jobs and other users processes. Essential for discovering scheduled tasks, running services, and credential exposure in process arguments. The go-to tool for finding privesc via cron jobs.
notes:
=== DOWNLOAD ===
  # Pre-compiled binaries:
  # 64-bit: pspy64
  # 32-bit: pspy32
  # Small versions: pspy64s, pspy32s

=== BASIC USAGE ===
  chmod +x pspy64
  ./pspy64
  # Monitors all processes in real-time
  # Watch for cron jobs, backup scripts, etc.

=== WHAT TO LOOK FOR ===
  # Cron jobs running as root:
  # CMD: UID=0  | /bin/bash /opt/backup.sh
  # Scripts with credentials:
  # CMD: UID=0  | mysql -u root -pSecretPass
  # Writable scripts called by root:
  # CMD: UID=0  | /tmp/cleanup.sh
  # Services restarting:
  # CMD: UID=0  | systemctl restart apache2

=== COLOR OUTPUT ===
  ./pspy64 -pf -i 1000
  # -pf = print commands AND file system events
  # -i 1000 = scan every 1 second

=== COMMON PRIVESC PATHS ===
  1. Root cron job executes writable script -> modify script
  2. Root cron job uses writable directory -> path hijack
  3. Credentials visible in process arguments
  4. Root cron job with wildcard injection opportunity
  5. Root process loading libraries from writable path

recommended.note: LinPEAS for comprehensive privesc enumeration; pspy for process monitoring.

defense.why_it_works: pspy uses Linux procfs and inotify to monitor process creation. Since /proc is readable by all users and inotify watches are unprivileged, no root access is needed to observe all processes.
defense.prerequisites: User access on Linux system; pspy binary uploaded.
defense.impact: Reveals cron jobs, credentials in process arguments, and running services without root.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1057] inotify watches on /proc; pspy binary execution; high-frequency /proc scanning.
defense.artifacts: pspy binary on disk; inotify watch creation; /proc directory access patterns.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=linux sourcetype=syslog process_name="pspy*"
| table _time, host, user, process
defense.sentinel_kql:
Syslog
| where ProcessName has "pspy"
| project TimeGenerated, HostName, ProcessName, SyslogMessage
defense.prevention: Monitor for pspy binary names; hidepid mount option on /proc; limit inotify watches; restrict binary uploads.

detections.name: pspy process monitoring tool execution
detections.logic:
title: pspy Process Monitoring Tool
status: experimental
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - /pspy64
      - /pspy32
      - /pspy64s
      - /pspy32s
  condition: selection
level: high
detections.false_positives: Renamed pspy binary will evade filename detection
detections.tuning: Also detect by behavior: high-frequency inotify watches on /proc
